description: We are a group of Computer Science and Engineering students who are passionate about identifying and solving real-world problem in our environment. Rather than building projects just for the sake of it, we focus on spotting genuine pain points around us; in our communities, campuses, and everyday lives; and applying technology to address them meaningfully
summary: Sankofa is a crop-rotation decision-support tool for Ghanaian smallholder farmers. It scores rotation strategies against farmer-defined priorities: soil health, water availability, and market value using NASA POWER climate records, MODIS NDVI vegetation trends, ISRIC SoilGrids soil data, and FAO GAEZ crop suitability data. A deterministic scoring engine produces transparent, traceable recommendations. Gemini 3.5 Flash explains those scores in plain English; Khaya AI translates them into 7 Ghanaian languages. Sankofa assists farmer judgment, it never replaces it.
details:
Sankofa is a web-based crop rotation decision-support tool that combines satellite climate data, vegetation indices, and soil science to help Ghanaian smallholder farmers decide what to plant next season.
How it works
Farmers enter their location (via GPS or place name search), their current crop, and their priorities across three factors: water availability, soil health, and market value. Sankofa queries NASA POWER for 24 years of daily rainfall data, computes the rainfall onset date using a 10-day rolling sum algorithm, and retrieves MODIS NDVI vegetation health trends for that location. ISRIC SoilGrids supplies soil texture, pH, organic carbon, and nitrogen data at 250m resolution. FAO GAEZ provides crop suitability scores by agro-ecological zone.
A deterministic scoring engine combines these into a composite score for each candidate rotation across Water, Soil, Suitability, Market, and Risk sub-scores. The farmer’s current practice is always shown first as a baseline; alternatives must score at least 0.2 points higher to appear. Every score traces directly to a specific NASA indicator and a specific crop, no black boxes.
Gemini 3.5 Flash narrates the scores in plain language. Khaya AI then translates that narration into the farmer’s chosen language across 7 Ghanaian languages including Twi, Ewe, Ga, Fante, Dagbani, Gurene, and Kusaal. The AI explains the ranking, it never changes it.
Key features
Rainfall scenario slider (Low/Normal/High) re-scores all cards live, letting farmers simulate drought or flood conditions before committing.
Priority toggles allow farmers to weight what matters most to them personally.
A Sankofa Stat banner shows exactly how the rainfall season has shifted at the farmer’s coordinates over 24 years.
A colour-coded NDVI bar chart shows vegetation health trends over 5 years.
An agro-ecological zone map contextualizes recommendations within Ghana’s three distinct farming zones.
Pest and risk warnings localized to each rotation and season.
Data confidence labels on every card explicitly flag soil interpolation distance, resolution limits, and missing market price data.
Every recommendation includes a prompt to verify with a MoFA (Ministry of Food and Agriculture) extension officer.
Impact
Sankofa targets Ghana’s farming community, whose rotation decisions have historically relied on generational knowledge now disrupted by climate change. By translating NASA satellite data into plain-language, locally relevant recommendations in a farmer’s own language, Sankofa bridges the gap between space-based earth observation and ground-level agricultural decision-making. The same NASA POWER and MODIS pipeline is applicable across West Africa with no architectural changes.
Tools and technologies
Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, React-Leaflet, Recharts.
Backend: Python, FastAPI, deployed on Railway. Frontend deployed on Vercel.
Data sources: NASA POWER API, MODIS NDVI, ISRIC SoilGrids, FAO GAEZ, OSM Nominatim.
AI: Gemini 3.5 Flash (narration), Khaya AI Translation API v2 (localisation).
